findings.title: F8 verification: compile location of StageServerPortProbe/StageServerStartResult is unspecified, so the test may still not compile
findings.problem: The design proves WorshipPlayer.Tests (net8.0, Core-only reference) cannot see StageDisplayServer.cs, but never says which file declares StageServerPortProbe and StageServerStartResult. If declared inside StageDisplayServer.cs (where StartAsync consults them), the test cannot compile against them — the exact problem the design meant to avoid.
findings.fix: State that StageServerPortProbe and the StageServerStartResult record live in their own new source file(s) added to the Tests project's <Compile Include> set (Link'd like the others), OR in WorshipPlayer.Core which the test already references. Call out that adding a <Compile Include> entry changes the test csproj and must be re-checked against the no-new-warnings / 411-green invariant.
findings.resolution: Fix F8 Decision 4 commits both StageServerPortProbe and the StageServerStartResult record to WorshipPlayer.Core (not inside StageDisplayServer.cs, which StageDisplayServer consumes). Verified WorshipPlayer.Tests.csproj has a single ProjectReference to WorshipPlayer.Core and its <Compile Include> set does NOT include StageDisplayServer.cs, so the Core placement makes the F8 test compile with no new <Compile Include> entry. Any csproj change must keep 0 new warnings beyond the 4 pre-existing and all tests green.

findings.title: F8 start-result path must not dereference null _presenterSettings/_remoteCommandHandler on the single-arg constructor production uses
findings.problem: PresenterIntegration constructs the server via new StageDisplayServer(StageServerPort) (single-arg), leaving _remoteCommandHandler and _presenterSettings null. The F8 rewrite of StartAsync/StageServerStartResult does not state it must work on this instance; if the new observe/start logic reads those null fields it will NRE in production while a 4-arg-constructor test passes.
findings.fix: Add a constraint to Fix F8: the StartAsync -> StageServerStartResult path must not dereference _presenterSettings or _remoteCommandHandler (both may be null on the single-arg constructor). Add a unit test calling StartAsync on a single-arg-constructed server asserting a clean StageServerStartResult with no NRE.
findings.resolution: Fix F8 Decision 5 forbids the StartAsync -> StageServerStartResult path from dereferencing _presenterSettings, _remoteCommandHandler, or _presenterEngine (all null on the single-arg constructor StageDisplayServer(int port = 5055, ...) — verified). Verification plan F8 (c) adds a unit test that calls StartAsync on a single-arg-constructed server and asserts a clean StageServerStartResult with no NullReferenceException.

findings.title: F5 verification under-specified: no named extractable method, no transpose sign/compose-order convention
findings.problem: Fix F5 says 'extract the text-building into a testable method' without naming it or giving a signature, and does not define whether a +N semitone pitch shift transposes chords up by N or how capo/nashville compose with the pitch offset on congregation output. The engine already has GetStageText(slide, transposeSemitones); the design does not say whether output reuses it.
findings.fix: Name the extracted method and signature (or reuse PresenterEngine.GetStageText) in a location the Tests project can compile, and state the convention: congregation output applies Transpose(text, +pitchSemitones) only when ShowChords is true; pitch 0 returns text unchanged; capo/nashville remain stage-only. Add a concrete unit assertion (e.g. [C] at +2 -> [D]).
findings.resolution: Fix F5 commits to reusing the existing PresenterEngine.GetStageText(Slide slide, int transposeSemitones) (verified present and linked into WorshipPlayer.Tests via PresenterEngine.cs). Convention committed: congregation output applies Transpose(text, +pitchSemitones) only when ShowChords is true; +N = up; pitch 0 returns text unchanged; capo/nashville remain stage-only. Verification plan F5 adds the concrete assertion [C] at +2 -> [D] and 0 -> unchanged.

findings.title: F12 snapshot field count wrong (seven vs ten actual reads)
findings.problem: Fix F12 says BroadcastStageUpdate reads SEVEN engine members, but it actually reads ten (CurrentSlide.Content.Text, NextSlide.Content.Text, CurrentSlide.SectionName, CurrentSong.Title, CurrentSong.OriginalKey twice, IsLive, IsBlacked, CurrentSlideIndex, TotalSlides). The torn-read concern is valid but the enumeration omits CurrentSong.Title/OriginalKey.
findings.fix: Update the F12 member list to the ten actually read and have SnapshotStageData() derive SongTitle/Key/OriginalKey from _currentSong under the same lock.
findings.resolution: Fix F12 now lists the TEN members actually read by BroadcastStageUpdate (verified): CurrentSlide.Content.Text, NextSlide.Content.Text, CurrentSlide.SectionName, CurrentSong.Title, CurrentSong.OriginalKey (read twice as Key and OriginalKey), IsLive, IsBlacked, CurrentSlideIndex, TotalSlides. SnapshotStageData() reads _currentSong.Title/_currentSong.OriginalKey under the same _stateLock, and LoadSong's _currentSong write takes that lock.

findings.title: F1 startup auto-load should state its interaction with the backtrack song-load/stem-preload path
findings.problem: Auto-loading the most recent service on startup sets the first item current; if that item is a backtrack Song, OnServiceItemChanged fires SongLoadRequested and preloads stems that this worktree's Songs/ folder lacks. The design does not state this must degrade silently rather than error on startup.
findings.fix: Specify that ServiceOrderLoaded handling sets the first item current but any resulting SongLoadRequested/stem load is wrapped by MainWindow.LoadSong's existing try/catch, and add a human check: on startup with the sample service and missing stems the app fills the sidebar and shows a non-fatal 'stems not found' status rather than erroring.
findings.resolution: Fix F1 commits that ServiceOrderLoaded setting the first item current may trigger a backtrack SongLoadRequested/stem preload, which degrades silently through MainWindow.LoadSong's existing try/catch (non-fatal 'stems not found' status) and does NOT error on startup; the handler adds no throwing wrapper of its own. Verification plan F1 adds the human startup-degrade check.
